item.title: GTA 6 reportedly sets massive livestreaming record, watched more in its first week than Elden Ring, Diablo 4, Valorant, and Lost Ark combined
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record. After attracting more viewers across livestreaming platforms than any game ever on its launch day, Rockstar's open-world crime sim has reportedly continued to dominate on platforms like Twitch , YouTube, and Kick. Read more
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record. After attracting more viewers across livestreaming platforms than any game ever on its launch day, Rockstar's open-world crime sim has reportedly continued to dominate on platforms like Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.
Over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts. That's nearly three times more than the previous record, held by Valorant's closed beta in April 2020. In fact, that 420m hours tally is more than the first-week watch time achieved by Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo 4, and Lost Ark combined.
As for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed. In fact, Twitch's GTA 6 watch time was higher at launch than any other game in its history.
Streams Charts also noted 1,056 channels reached new all-time peak viewership numbers while streaming GTA 6, in some cases multiplying their previous record tenfold. Major content creators like IShowSpeed, IlloJuan, and TheBurntPeanut stole the spotlight, but GTA 6 also helped many other channels set new viewership records.
Livestreaming, of course, isn't the only area where GTA 6 has set new records. Publisher Take-Two called it the biggest entertainment launch in history, generating $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue from 32.5m copies sold on day one. Other parts of the industry have benefited, too. Anticipation for GTA 6 boosted US hardware sales for both PlayStation and Xbox, just as GTA 6 became each console brand's most pre-ordered title ever. At launch, more than 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5, according to Sony. The game also had the highest number of concurrent players ever on any PlayStation console, beating even the most popular free-to-play titles.
You can check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough if you're in need of assistance, which we just updated today with a guide on how to whistle in GTA 6 - something I didn't know you could do. The walkthrough also covers other lesser-known mechanics such as how to steal ATMs in GTA 6, and much more besides.

item.title: Lucia actress Manni L. Perez claims she worked on GTA 6 for ‘almost a decade’
item.summary: Manni L. Perez thanks GTA 6 fans for their response to Lucia
item.text:
Actress Manni L. Perez has responded to Grand Theft Auto 6 fans after its “whirlwind” launch week.
Perez, who played Lucia in GTA 6, also gives us a better idea of when she started working with Rockstar. She says claims has been playing Lucia for “almost a decade” now, suggesting she was cast very early on in development.
“Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days, and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” Perez says on an Instagram story.
“Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received.
“I’ve dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She’s been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.”

item.title: Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system because its player agency 'was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from'
item.summary: "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up."
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director. With thousands of enterable buildings, unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs, and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.
"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun."
The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System.
"There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from."
Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.
"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money."
The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".

item.title: GTA 6 on Xbox One is a ‘remarkable feat’, according to analysis
item.summary: Analysis of GTA 6 on Xbox One shows that it can handle streaming the Series S port
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6’s Xbox One release has been described as a “remarkable feat” in a new performance analysis.
This comes from Digital Foundry’s testing of the Xbox One release of GTA 6, which works by streaming the Xbox Series S release of the game.
Their findings suggest that Xbox has allocated additional resources to GTA 6 streaming, as the quality was found to be “significantly” better than other games available via streaming.
“I don’t think there’s any argument that this is the cheapest entry point to playing the game,” says Thomas Morgan from Digital Foundry. “So, the question is whether it’s good enough for most people to just jump in.
“It’s a remarkable feat what Microsoft has achieved here in terms of the architecture they’ve set up server-side to make this possible, and to mitigate the issues in latency and compression to such a point that actually I wasn’t as bothered by either of those issues as much as I thought I would be going in.”
In side-by-side shots, we see that while the image is blurrier on Xbox One than on Xbox Series S, you usually have to look very carefully to notice the differences. They also find that the motion blur does a good job of hiding these differences.
“There wasn’t really any perceptible loss in playing the game [on Xbox One],” Morgan says. “Obviously, I’ve got it set to 1440p and that’s not the native resolution being beamed over via Series S, but it gives it the best possible opportunity to give us the highest bit rate and bandwidth.”
Digital Foundry also praised Xbox’s work in reducing input delays, with Morgan saying it was easy to forget he was streaming the game, rather than playing it natively.
Furthermore, the frame rate from Xbox One and Series S is described as “one to one”, without many differences in terms of performance. They did, however, find frame pacing issues on Xbox One, so it won’t be quite as smooth as Series S, even when it does reach 30fps.
All in all, most of the issues outside of frame pacing are ones that you would find on Xbox Series S. Digital Foundry’s analysis of the Series S found that it was a strong effort, but noted that there were more frame rate drops than on other platforms. Still, these releases make for a much cheaper entry point for anyone looking to pick up GTA 6.

item.title: Where to find GTA 6's UFO and alien
item.summary: Get down with the extraterrestrial.
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 might feel more grounded compared to its predecessors, but that doesn't mean Leonida isn't full of weird and supernatural ongoings. One such paranormal activity is GTA 6's aliens—if you know where to look, you'll be able to find a UFO which'll eventually lead you down a strange road of cows, radiation, and the aliens themselves.
And if you don't know where to look, here's where I can help you. If you want to find GTA 6's UFO and a weird little alien guy, here's exactly where you need to go and what you need to do.
The alien abduction is actually a three-parter mission, and to get started you'll first need to locate the abandoned car. You'll need to look for it at nighttime, and it can spawn in a number of locations. For me, it was a little ways east of Port Gellhorn in Kelly County. For our own Chris Livingston, he discovered the car somewhere north of Capri, also in Kelly County. You know it's the one if the car is pointed toward a forest and the doors are open.
Once you've found it, you'll need to follow the path it's parked along. You'll know you're going the right way by the clothes strewn along the path. If it's a bit too dark or you're stuck, you can press L3 + R3 to activate your focus and see the clothes more easily or equip your flashlight. Eventually you'll see the lights of the UFO and a very naked lady amongst it all. Head over until a cutscene plays out.
Once that's over, you'll get into a light scuffle with the woman before she instructs you to go get her car. Head back to where you first found the vehicle, where one more cutscene will play out and you'll be done… for now.
You'll need to wait for some time to pass. Make sure you're heading home and going to sleep each night, preferably as whichever character you discovered the UFO on. Eventually, you'll trigger a cutscene that'll bring you to a white room.

item.title: GTA 6 Developers Have Voted Against Unionization by 75% to 25%
item.summary: Rockstar Games workers have rejected a union deal with the IWGB as Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks records
item.text:
Rockstar Games' UK workforce has voted firmly against unionization the week after the studio's latest game, Grand Theft Auto 6, demolished sales records.
The vote was 25% in favor of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. It's a decisive result, especially considering a 93.2% turnout for the vote, with 1,544 employees from Rockstar's offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating.
The two-week ballot coincided not just with GTA 6's launch, but with an employment tribunal hearing over the firing of 31 Rockstar workers in 2025. Rockstar argued the workers had leaked company secrets, while the IWGB characterized the action as union-busting. A judgment in the case is pending.
The union can continue to represent individual members, and Rockstar staff remain free to organize over pay, overtime, and other issues, but Rockstar management will not be formally required to meet or negotiate with union reps.
Rockstar Games head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement that the company was "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6."
"This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together."
In its own statement, the IWGB vowed to fight on. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union said. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen."

item.title: South Park Finale Puts Kenny Inside GTA 6
item.summary: Kenny crawls out of the boys’ TV while they play GTA 6 in the South Park finale, giving the season’s running gag a horror movie punchline.
item.text:
South Park spent its entire 29th season joking about Grand Theft Auto VI and the finale paid it off with Kenny crawling out of the game. In "City Endings," which aired November 25 on Comedy Central, the boys sit down to play GTA 6, spot Kenny lying on a sidewalk and realize they forgot about him, right before he drags himself toward the screen and bursts out of the TV like something out of The Ring.
Just to be clear, Kenny is not in GTA 6 as an Easter Egg, whatever the viral clip's caption suggests. The sequence is South Park dropping its own dead kid into gameplay it shows on screen.
As we've mentioned, this was the payoff for a season that started with a town that kept insisting things would get better in November, the show's stand-in for the release date. Episode 2 turned a blackout into a GTA 6 save-data crisis. By Episode 4 the show was airing real GTA 6 footage straight from Rockstar Games, Jason on the beach and all, confirmed in the credits. "City Endings" is the last beat of a joke built across the whole season.
The plot around it is pure South Park. With the whole town glued to GTA 6, rolling outages hit. The boys trace them to Mayor McDaniels' secret deal with the "billionaire weenies" whose AI data centers are draining the grid, while the town's politicians hunt for a scapegoat, pointing to GTA VI instead. Kenny's spirit cannot rest until the corruption comes out, so his horror-show breakout is what pushes the kids to act. By the end the power is back and Kenny is too.
The joke works because it is barely a joke. GTA 6 is the kind of event South Park used to save for elections. The show treated its launch in the same way, a date the whole country counted down to and a blackout when it arrived. The game's record-breaking launch gave the writers the perfect thing to unplug.
South Park is only the latest corner of pop culture to rebuild itself around GTA 6 this month. NBA 2K27 turned its online hub into a neon Vice City, the soundtrack took over Spotify and the boxed edition set physical sales records across Europe without a disc inside. A cartoon town losing power while everyone is playing it is the most honest version of that story yet.
Kenny always comes back. This time he had to crawl out of GTA 6 to get anyone to look up from the controller.

item.title: Rockstar Developer Explains How Players Should Experience GTA VI
item.summary: According to a recent report by Kotaku, Rockstar Games wants Grand Theft Auto VI players to experience the world of Leonida without constantly worrying about completing tasks or reaching 100% completion. According to the game’s Vice President of Design, Stephen Donkin, players should take their time and discover things naturally instead of treating the game [...] The post Rockstar Developer Explains How Players Should Experience GTA VI appeared first on RockstarINTEL .
item.text:
According to a recent report by Kotaku, Rockstar Games wants Grand Theft Auto VI players to experience the world of Leonida without constantly worrying about completing tasks or reaching 100% completion. According to the game’s Vice President of Design, Stephen Donkin, players should take their time and discover things naturally instead of treating the game like a checklist.
In a set of development notes shared with the press, Donkin explained that there is so much to do and discover in Leonida that he hopes players will eventually stop thinking about tasks, completion percentages and online guides.
He also explained that exploring the world at your own pace can make the experience feel almost infinite. While Leonida feels incredibly large, Donkin believes that individual encounters still feel carefully handcrafted, with a human touch behind them. Donkin’s first Rockstar Games credit was as a QA tester on Grand Theft Auto V. His comments also give an insight into how the studio approaches world design and player exploration.
GTA VI Also Has Quiet and Relaxing Moments
Senior Design Director Ghyan Koehne also shared his thoughts about the different experiences found throughout GTA VI. According to him, the game features plenty of high-energy moments, action, thrills and humor. However, he also mentioned quieter and more meditative experiences that offer a completely different feeling.
When asked to describe the feeling Rockstar wants players to experience with a single word, Koehne chose “wonder.” He explained that the studio wants players to constantly experience this feeling and go through a mixture of emotions throughout the game.
Donkin also shared what he hopes players feel while exploring Leonida. He explained that players who let themselves become immersed in the world and simply follow their curiosity can experience Leonida in the same way he did during development.
These comments offer an interesting perspective on how Rockstar approaches open-world games. Instead of focusing entirely on completing objectives and finding everything through online guides, the studio encourages players to explore at their own pace.
With GTA VI having been out for a week now, players have already started exploring Leonida and discovering its many details. As Donkin explained, sometimes the best way to experience the game is simply to follow your curiosity.
